name: Idempotent Consumer
problem: Every reliable delivery mechanism available — broker redelivery, outbox relay, client retry, saga compensation — is at-least-once. A consumer that assumes single delivery produces duplicate aggregates or inconsistent state the first time a failover occurs.
forces: Exactly-once delivery is not achievable; exactly-once effect is, and only at the consumer.
Deduplication state must be durable for at least as long as the redelivery window.
The deduplication key must be supplied by the producer or derived deterministically, never generated on receipt.
solution: Every consumer implements idempotency using a deduplicated message key. The key identifies the logical operation, not the delivery attempt. A repeated key produces the recorded outcome without re-executing the handler.

appliesTo.guidance: Consumers declare hasIdempotencyKey=true in event-driven.config.json. Enforced by ED-R05.
Event consumers must handle duplicate delivery gracefully; cross-module ordering is only best-effort.
Applies to mutating HTTP endpoints as well as to event handlers, since retries reach both.
Managed event sources retry on any non-success result, making duplicate invocation routine.

variants.name: Idempotency-key middleware
variants.invariant: A client-supplied key is recorded with its response and replayed verbatim on repeat, without invoking the handler.

variants.name: Consumer-side deduplication store
variants.invariant: Processed message keys are persisted and checked before handling.

relationships.note: The outbox is the most common source of the duplicates this pattern absorbs.

governedBy.title: Message Bus Delivery & Flow Control Strategy
governedBy.note: Section 6 of the ADR records an 'Idempotent Consumer Mandate'.

enforcedBy.statement: All event consumers MUST implement idempotency using a deduplicated message key (hasIdempotencyKey=true in event-driven.config.json).
